title: UFO Moviez Launches 'Blessings' Ahead of Ramayana: Part 1

Ahead of the Diwali release of Ramayana: Part 1, UFO Moviez has launched “Blessings”, a campaign inviting brands and advertising agencies to participate in the cultural and theatrical excitement surrounding the film.

Scheduled for worldwide release on 5 November 2026, Ramayana: Part 1 brings the story of Lord Ram to cinemas during India’s biggest festive season. The campaign draws from the faith, family values and traditions associated with Ramayana and gives brands an opportunity to become part of a shared experience that will bring audiences across generations into cinema halls.

At the heart of the campaign is a simple question: “This Diwali, millions will seek ‘Blessings’. Will your brand be there?”

Through “Blessings”, brands can build visibility throughout the film’s theatrical journey, beginning before its release and continuing through the festive and cinema-going period. UFO Moviez will support the campaign through its social-media platforms, audience insights, participating brand associations, cinema activations and campaign highlights. This will allow advertisers to extend their presence beyond the cinema screen and participate in the wider conversations generated by the film.

Featuring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Sunny Deol, Ravi Dubey and Arun Govil, Ramayana: Part 1 presents the iconic story through a large-scale cinematic production. Trade projections place the film’s potential worldwide box-office collection at more than ₹2,000 crore, while its India release is targeting over 9,000 screens. Recent successes such as Hanuman Ansh, Kantara and Mahavatar Narsimha have also shown the strong audience interest in stories rooted in Indian culture and tradition.

According to ProCAT, UFO Moviez’s cinema intelligence platform, the film’s trailer has generated more than one billion views across languages and platforms. With a reported worldwide release target of nearly 50,000 screens, the film has the potential to create conversations well beyond cinema halls. ProCAT also estimates more than 125 million potential theatrical footfalls across India during the film’s cinema run.

UFO Moviez holds long-term advertising rights across more than 4,000 screens in over 1,200 cities and towns, covering premium multiplexes as well as popular single-screen cinemas. Through one platform, brands can use this network to reach audiences across metropolitan, urban and regional India during the Diwali period.

Advertisers can participate through five levels of campaign ownership. Presence offers on-screen advertising across Ramayana shows, while Impact includes premium anamorphic formats and high-visibility advertising positions. Experience combines on-screen visibility with lobby activations, kiosks and photobooths. Takeover offers dominant visibility across selected cinema properties, while the 360° option brings cinema, on-ground experiences and social-media amplification together in one customised campaign.

The opportunity is relevant to fast-moving consumer goods, banking and financial services, automobiles, jewellery, smartphones, consumer durables, electronic commerce, travel and other categories seeking increased brand visibility during the festive season.

Sachinn Guptaa, Country Head – Enterprise Business, UFO Moviez, said, “Ramayana brings together cultural relevance, family appeal and the scale of a major theatrical event. Its Diwali release gives brands an opportunity to connect with audiences during a meaningful shared experience and strengthen their visibility during the country’s most important festive season.”

“With the film targeting more than 9,000 screens in India and UFO Moviez offering advertising access across over 4,000 screens, brands can participate at scale through one platform. ‘Blessings’ offers advertisers several ways to engage audiences, ranging from on-screen visibility to immersive cinema experiences and integrated campaigns. For brands seeking attention, reach and festive relevance, this campaign can become a true blessing.”
